title: Capability topology and authority lattice for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design the RBAC v2 role model focused on a capability-oriented topology and authority lattice that maps cleanly to Redwood Inference resource hierarchies (organization -> tenant -> project -> model -> route). Must include scope semantics, permission derivation rules, admin controls (breakglass and delegated admin), SSO/SAML claim mapping, and audit logging hooks. Deliver a migration-safe plan, compatibility shims for legacy RBAC, and an operational rollout strategy with feature flags and metrics.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Clear role/permission schema document that maps to resource hierarchy and includes precedence rules (deny/allow, specificity).
A2: Prototype ACL resolver implemented in runtime-auth service with unit tests and end-to-end policy evaluation tests.
A3: Audit log schema defined and wired to operations pipelines (events for grant/revoke/eval with actor, resource, action, decision, policy_id).
A4: SSO/SAML claim mapping spec with examples for IdP>Redwood transformation and test vectors for Okta and AzureAD.
A5: Migration path documented with compatibility layer and a feature-flagged rollout plan to avoid customer disruption.
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Kickoff. Problem statement: current RBAC lacks fine-grained scope binding across multi-tenant resource fabrics and doesn't express time-limited or context-bound capabilities (eg. can-start-job-with-quota). Goal: role model that supports capability composition, safe inheritance, and explainable evaluation for audits.

2026-03-11 Miguel Santos: Initial draft of authority lattice: we represent privileges as (action, resource-pattern, condition-set). Authority nodes are immutable tuples with a stable policy_id. We'll add canonicalization rules for resource-patterns to avoid duplicate policies.

2026-03-12 Design review (Carla Nguyen): Prefer explicit allow/deny with deny taking precedence. Suggested adding 'delegation' flag to authorities to indicate if that grant can be regranted. Also requested examples for edge-case: cross-tenant read-only access for support SREs.

2026-03-12 Security review (Ravi Patel): Need to ensure audit logs capture policy provenance and SAML mapping events. Asked for retention guidance and KMS tagging for logs containing PII references. Marked as security_review_required.

2026-03-13 Engineering notes: Prototype resolver implemented in branch feature/authz-lattice. Key trade-offs: (1) Evaluate at runtime vs precomputed bitsets — chosen hybrid: precompute index for common tenant-model prefixes, fallback resolver for rare patterns. (2) Token size for grant claims — keep short policy_id references rather than full policy definitions in tokens.

2026-03-13 Migration discussion: We'll implement a compatibility shim that translates legacy role bindings into the new authority nodes at read time. Migration steps: export existing bindings -> canonicalize -> place behind feature flag 'authz.v2' per tenant -> gradual enable. Must include a revert plan and telemetry to detect auth regressions.

2026-03-14 SSO/SAML mapping: Proposed claim map: 'groups' -> potential role seeds; recommended IdP attribute 'redwood_roles' for direct role assertions (for enterprise customers). Example Okta mapping added in design doc (link in PR). Need solution for SCIM provisioning to keep role assignments synchronized.

2026-03-14 Audit logging hooks: Events to emit: policy.created, policy.updated, binding.granted, binding.revoked, access.eval (decision). Each event includes actor_id, actor_email, ip, timestamp, resource_pattern, action, decision, policy_id, evaluation_trace (list of policy_ids evaluated). For large traces, store trace_id and push detailed trace to internal audit-store. Asked infra to confirm retention quotas.

2026-03-14 Notes on admin controls: Breakglass flow design — emergency API that issues a time-limited elevated grant with strong IAM approvals (2-person) and an automatic revocation anchor. All breakglass ops are high-urgency audit events and require out-of-band notification to on-call Slack channel + PagerDuty.
implementation_notes: Resolver: implement authority-lattice resolver in runtime-auth; use prefix tree for resource-pattern indices.

Policy model: store immutable policy documents with policy_id; policy documents reference action sets (strings), resource patterns, conditions (time-window, IP allowlist, quota checks), and delegation flag.
Evaluation: deny takes precedence. Evaluation algorithm returns (decision, matched_policies[], trace_id). Provide explain endpoint for 'why denied/allowed'.
Caching: precompute tenant-level allow bitsets for top 500 patterns; use KV cache with invalidation on policy change.
Audit: emit structured JSON events to audit-stream: topic 'authz-events'. For access.eval collapse large traces into trace_id referencing audit-store entry.

SSO: accept both group->role heuristics and direct role claims. Provide mapping UI in Console for admin to map IdP groups to Redwood authorities. SCIM sync to mirror assignment changes when available.
samples_and_cheatsheet: Resource hierarchy: organization:{org_id} -> tenant:{tenant_id} -> project:{project_id} -> model:{model_id} -> route:{route_id}

Example authority nodes (text):
- policy_id: pol_001; description: 'model:read'; actions: [read]; resource_pattern: 'tenant:{t}/project:{p}/model:{m}'; deny: false; delegation: false
- policy_id: pol_002; description: 'model:deploy'; actions: [deploy]; resource_pattern: 'tenant:{t}/project:{p}/model:{m}'; deny: false; delegation: true
- policy_id: pol_900; description: 'support:cross-tenant-read'; actions: [read]; resource_pattern: 'tenant:* /project:* /model:*'; deny: true; exception: ['support-team-namespace'] (deny exception semantics handled via explicit allow).

Permission derivation rules:
1) Match resource_pattern by most-specific pattern (longest prefix).
2) Aggregate all matched policies for the actor (direct bindings, group->role, token claims).
3) If any matched policy has deny=true -> decision=deny.
4) Else if any allow -> decision=allow.
5) Conditions (time-window, quota) applied last; failure results in deny with condition code.

SSO mapping examples:
- Okta groups claim -> map to set of policy_ids using Console mapping UI.
- SAML assertion 'redwood_roles' -> comma-separated policy_ids for direct assignment.
- SCIM provisioning will write bindings via admin API to keep authoritative state.
migration_plan: Step 0: Audit current bindings and export counts by tenant (who has what).
Step 1: Implement canonicalizer that converts legacy role names to authority nodes (one-time transformational mapping).
Step 2: Deploy authz-lattice with compatibility shim behind 'authz.v2' feature flag default=false for all tenants.
Step 3: Enable for internal tenants and run shadow-eval for 2 weeks, log discrepancies to 'authz-migration' dashboard.
Step 4: Invite pilot customers to opt-in; iterate on mapping heuristics and fix false-deny cases.
Step 5: Gradual ramp to 100% with telemetry checks and automated rollback policy if error rate > 0.1% auth failures for a 24h window.
